verdict.reasoning: Patient reports a new headache starting yesterday mid-morning, located on the left side at the back: 'It started yesterday... About mid-morning.' and 'It's on the left side at the back.'
Headache described as throbbing, gradual onset, intensity 8/10: 'just quite, intense, and kinda quite throbbing. It kind of built up gradually' and 'I'd say about eight.'

Patient denies nausea, vomiting, visual changes, photophobia, neuro deficits, or positional change: 'No, nothing.' to nausea/vomiting/tingling/numbness/weakness; 'No.' to blurred vision or pain over eyes; 'No...No.' to funny lights and light sensitivity; 'Um, no.' to positional differences.

Normal sleep and eating/drinking, reduced ability to work: 'Yes, yes, like normal.' (eating/drinking) and 'Uh, yes I did.' (sleep through night) and 'I don't feel that, I'm finding it really hard to , to do any of, my work, or, normal things.'
Tried ibuprofen (Nurofen) yesterday with little effect: 'I took some, um, um, Nurofen, yesterday.' and 'Not really.' when asked if it made any difference.
Patient reports no other medical problems: 'have you got any other medical problems?' 'Um, no I haven't.' This supports no known past medical history in the transcript.
Transcript only documents a one-time use of ibuprofen: 'No, only the, Nurofen I took yesterday, Ibuprofen.' It does not support ongoing PRN use.

When asked about over-the-counter medications or allergies, patient mentions only Nurofen and does not report any allergies: 'Um, any over-the-counter medications or allergies?' 'No, only the, Nurofen I took yesterday.' This supports no reported allergies in the transcript.
Family history: 'my mother's had hypertension, and she does get migraines.'
'Who do you live with at home?' 'My partner.' and 'I'm a designer.' confirms living with partner and occupation as designer.
Social history: 'And do you smoke at all normally?' 'No I don't.' 'Do you drink any alcohol regularly?' 'No.' 'Um, and any other drugs?' 'No.'

Transcript documents an acute unilateral throbbing headache with no red-flag symptoms: left-sided, throbbing, new since yesterday, no fever, rash, vomiting, neuro deficits, vision changes, or positional component. While the diagnostic label 'likely primary (migraine versus tension)' is an interpretation, it is a reasonable clinical inference from the provided data and no red-flag features were noted or discussed.

Doctor advises stronger NSAID, not with ibuprofen, plus paracetamol: 'trying a slightly stronger, pain relief. Uh, so, similar to Ibuprofen, but taking instead of Ibuprofen not at the same time' and 'You can take Paracetamol along with that.'
Advice given: 'Try and um, take rest, have lots of good hydration.'

Safety-netting: 'if the pain's getting worse, or you get new symptoms, fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness... or you keep getting episodes of the same type of thing, then we need to speak to you' and 'if it's getting worse or not settling in the next day or two. Then certainly give us a call back.' This supports seeking care if worse, with fever/rash/vomiting/neck stiffness, recurrent episodes, or not settling within about 1–2 days (~48 hours).
